generator: tools/sourcing (ato-sourcing) — regenerate with `cargo run -p ato-sourcing -- fetch`
readme: Committed sourcing snapshot: price, stock, lifecycle and compliance per (MPN, distributor).
WHY COMMITTED: CI must be deterministic and offline. A gate that queries a live API fails
when a distributor rate-limits, and gives a different answer on every run — which is also
exactly why hardware.yml's atopile picker is currently broken (it calls a remote parts API
from CI). The fetcher runs locally with credentials; CI only ever reads this file.
WHY JSON AND NOT SQLITE: this is reviewed in pull requests. A stock change or an EOL notice
should show up as a readable diff, which a binary database cannot do. Keys are sorted and
formatting is stable so diffs stay minimal.
PROVENANCE: every offer carries `source`. `api` means a distributor API returned it;
`manual-research` means a human read it off a product page, with the date. The two are never
merged, so a hand-entered figure can always be told apart from a retrieved one.

SOURCING_PENDING: a part with no offers MUST carry `sourcing_pending` with a reason and a date. The gap is then data rather than absence — a candidate nobody priced cannot hide in a missing key. A Hard-locked revision does not accept it.
COMPLIANCE: per IPC-1752A practice, a compliance claim is stored with the date it was made
and the regulation revision it refers to — not as a bare boolean. A RoHS 'yes' from 2019 is
not a statement about today's exemption list.
